header.running_head: Relationships between Men, Women and Children

blocks.text: The Services that the Ansaar Youth and the Sahabah (RA) Rendered to Rasulullaah ﷺ
Hadhrat Anas (RA) narrates that there were twenty youngsters from the Ansaar who always stuck close to Rasulullaah ﷺ. Rasulullaah ﷺ would always dispatch them whenever he needed something done. [^1]
Hadhrat Abdur Rahmaan bin Auf (RA) reports that there were always four or five Sahabah (RA) who never parted from Rasulullaah ﷺ (when on journey) or from Rasulullaah ﷺ's door (when at home). [^2]

Hadhrat Abu Sa'eed Khudri (RA) relates, "We used to take turns (to be at Rasulullaah ﷺ's service) so that we could fulfil any need he had or he could dispatch us for any errand. Eventually, the people anticipating rewards (for this service) increased and there were plenty of people taking turns. As we were one day discussing Dajjaal, Rasulullaah ﷺ came out to ask, 'What are these whispered discussions all about? Have I not forbidden you from whispered discussion?'" [^3]

Hadhrat Assim bin Sufyaan says that it was either Hadhrat Abu Dardaa (RA) or Hadhrat Abu Dharr (RA) whom he heard say, "I once sought permission from Rasulullaah ﷺ to spend the night at his door so that he could awaken me for any need he may have. Rasulullaah ﷺ granted permission and I spent the night there." [^4]

Hadhrat Hudhayfah (RA) reports, "I once performed salaah with Rasulullaah ﷺ during the month of Ramadhaan. He then got up to take a bath and I screened him. When some water was left over in the container, he said, 'If you wish, you may use it to bath, otherwise, you may add some more water to it.' 'O Rasulullaah ﷺ!' I replied, 'This left-over water of yours is more beloved to me than anything more I may add.' When I then started to bath, Rasulullaah ﷺ screened me. 'You need not screen me,' I said. He replied, 'Why not? I must screen you just as you screened me.'" [^5]
Rasulullaah ﷺ's Relationship with his Son Ibraheem and other Children of his Family

Hadhrat Anas (RA) says, "I have never seen anyone more compassionate towards his family than Rasulullaah ﷺ. His son Ibraheem was given to a woman in the upper reaches of Madinah for suckling. With us in his company, Rasulullaah ﷺ used to go to the house, which would be filled with smoke because the nursing mother's husband was a blacksmith.
